scenes.heading: INT. YOUNG OLIVE’S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: A PARTY in FULL SWING. MOM and DAD SNOOK mingle amongst the
ADULT GUESTS. CAMERA FINDS YOUNG OLIVE standing in the doorway
wearing A PARTY DRESS, her HAIR twisted into perfect RINGLETS.
At this very moment, Young Olive Snook was 9
years, 39 weeks, 19 hours, 59 minutes old and
dressed to the nines. Though she looked the
picture of perfection, Young Olive felt the
very picture of neglect-ion.
CAMERA PUSHES IN ON OLIVE.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The party in full swing was the cause of her
parents’ current distraction...
She TUGS on her MOM’S DRESS. Mom and Dad pay her no mind.
Dejected, Young Olive gives up and walks away.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...but Young Olive learned a lesson long ago.
She learned her mother and father did not need a
diversion to be distracted from their daughter.

scenes.heading: EXT. YOUNG OLIVE’S HOUSE - PORCH - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Young Olive exits the house and sits down on the PORCH SWING.
Young Olive dreamed of a life where she was
actively loved and only occasionally ignored.
She picks up her JOCKEY HELMET, puts it on atop her curls. We
PUSH IN as Young Olive moves her JOCKEY GOGGLES over her eyes.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
As happens often with Olive Snook, her dreams
came true... just not quite how she intended.

scenes.heading: INT. CAR - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: TWO MEN, JERRY AND BUSTER, get into the front seat.
According to her parents’ testimony, Young Olive
Snook had been stolen away in a stolen vehicle
by dangerous car thieves and kidnappers, Jerry
Holmes and Roy “Buster” Bustamante.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 2.
CONTINUED:
Jerry HOT-WIRES THE CAR and drives away when Buster turns, spots
Olive. Buster turns back. PUSH IN as he (MOS) talks to Jerry.
A SERIES OF QUICK POPS:
-- Young Olive sits in the backseat of the moving car, her eyes
locked with Buster’s very serious (and menacing) gaze.
-- Young Olive sits on a couch in a DARK MOTEL ROOM. Jerry and
Buster, a PHONE RECEIVER held between them, are arguing b.g.
Their daughter was held for 1 day, 1 hour and
11 minutes before Jerry and Buster made their
first ransom call. Distraught and
heartbroken, Olive’s parents agreed to pay the
undisclosed sum and contacted the police.

scenes.heading: EXT. YOUNG OLIVE’S HOUSE - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Olive walks slowly toward the door, glances back at Jerry and
Buster, who follow a few steps behind.
The police, then, set a trap.
ANOTHER ANGLE - LOOKING UP finds Olive watching from a window.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
The little girl, slash future jockey, slash
pie waitress to-be, watched as her abductors
walked into the trap.
OLIVE’S POV - The kidnappers ARE HANDCUFFED, PUT INTO COP CARS.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Jerry Holmes and Buster Bustamante, convicted
in a court of law after a quick and speedy
trial, were sentenced to 25 years to life.
RESUME - OLIVE IN THE WINDOW. Mom and Dad appear on either side.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And Olive Snook learned a valuable lesson: “You
don’t know what you’ve got till it’s gone.”

scenes.heading: EXT. FIELD - NIGHT

lines.text: A tranquil country setting -- a FIELD OF FRESHLY-FALLEN SNOW.
26 years, 10 weeks, 3 days, 15 hours and 4
minutes -- or 8,264 hash marks on a wall --
later...
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 3.
CONTINUED:
CAMERA WIDENS TO REVEAL we are actually just outside the fence
of a PRISON that looms in the deep b.g. A beat, then, à la
“Raising Arizona,” Jerry, then Buster, BURST THROUGH THE SNOW
FROM UNDERGROUND.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...Jerry Holmes and Buster Bustamante busted
out of the Big House with only one person on
their mind: Olive Snook...
As they set off on foot...

scenes.heading: EXT. CLIFF - DAY (RE-USE FROM EPISODE 210, “THE NORWEGIANS”)

lines.text: Ned and Olive cling to a wispy branch on the side of the cliff.
...who was, at this very moment, hanging from
the Pie-Maker she loved who could never love
her, or so she thought.
I’m sorry you never saw me the way you see Chuck.
She looks up at him. He looks at her, hesitates, then:
I wouldn’t say “never.”
Confused, not by the particulars, but by this
particular usage...

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - KITCHEN - DAY

lines.text: PUSH IN ON OLIVE. She has several of Chuck’s books on
LINGUISTICS and currently pores over one titled: “The Double
Negative: What You Shouldn’t Not Know.”
...Olive read about sentence structure and the
use of the double negative...
NED holds up a forkful of food for Olive to sample.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...and with passive-aggressive panache,
broached the subject with the Pie-Maker.
I definitely don’t hate it.
What does that mean?
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 4.
CONTINUED:
Just what I said.
It means you like it?
You tell me.
Well, you said it wasn’t less tasty than the
Kick in the Kumquat, but more unfulfilling
than the Rock Me Amade-Quince.
(then)
I don’t like giving the pies funny names.
Does that not seem disrespectful?
There you go! You did it again.
What did I do again? Are you okay? You’ve
been acting a little unusual all day.
I think maybe I’ve got the post-traumatic
stress from the cliff dive that almost turned
us into canyon patties.
We’re safe now, Olive.
Yeah, but the whole thing keeps repeating on
me over and over, like a broken record or
Mexican food.
Olive gets an idea. As she CLIMBS UP ON A CHAIR...
OLIVE (CONT’D)
You know, they say the more you face the
trauma, the less power it has over you. It’s
called Cognitive Behavioral Therapy.
She kneels on the counter and REACHES UP and GRABS the BASE OF A
HYPERION LAMP HANGING FROM THE CEILING.
OLIVE (CONT’D)
Okay. So there we were, about to die and
taking what we’re sure will be our very last
breaths here on God’s green earth...
Olive, get down from there. You’re going to
hurt yourself.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 5.
CONTINUED: (2)
(in the moment)
That’s right, Ned. Oh, no. I’m slipping. I
can’t hold on much longer. If there’s anything
you wanna say to me before we meet the Big Man
at the Pearly Gates and check into the Hotel
Hereafter, now would be the time. And if you
could speak in the declarative only, with
affirmative or comparative modifiers, it’d make
things a lot easier for everybody.
CHUCK and EMERSON enter and Olive gets down and moves off.
Emerson and Chuck approach.
Ding dong, Daddy--
Emerson’s cut off by the FORKFUL OF PIE Ned sticks in his mouth.
EMERSON (CONT’D)
(savoring the pie)
Ding dong. That. Is heaven.
Pear-way to Heaven. It’s new. You know, now
that I’m out of the dead-waking and back to
just pie-baking and I don’t touch dead fruit
anymore, I can eat my own pies.
(takes a bite of pie)
Mmmm. I’m gonna get fat, aren’t I?
Ned considers that a moment, shrugs, takes another bite.
While you’re getting fat, there’s a dead lady
getting fished outta the Papen County Fountain
and I got a good feeling about it. Ambulance
siren’s blarin’ and I got my chasin’ shoes on.
Are you sure you don’t want to untie your
apron strings and lace up your chasing laces?
I’m sure. Ned is no longer waking the dead.
My apron is staying on, strings tied securely
in a double figure-eight follow through knot.
Then I, for one...
(pointedly, to Emerson)
-- and you should be, for two -- am supportive
of your decision. Because that’s what friends
are. Supportive.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 6.
CONTINUED: (3)
Looky-here. Yes, the zappity-zap nearly
turned everything into crappity-crap with Dead
Girl and her digging-up-Dead-Daddy ways.
I apologized for that.
“No” means “no.” I wanna lead a normal life
as a guy who just makes pie. Who wants to be
Superman? Not me. I say “no” to “Super” and
“yes” to “man.” From now on, I’m Clark Kent.
Well, that’s downright crap-tastic, Clark. I
now have an abnormally-large amount of work to
do since nobody’s waking up dead ladies
anymore so I can ask who killed ‘em.
And with that, Emerson heads for the door.

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - DINING AREA

lines.text: Chuck catches up with Emerson at the door:
What about me?
No conversation I ever wanna have begins with
those three words. I got work to do.
Work you don’t have to do alone. I know I’m
no Superman, but I’m smart and I’m helpful.
Maybe I could be your sidekick. I could be
the Alive-Again Avenger, who came back from
the dead to solve her own murder and stayed
back from the dead to bring justice to murder
victims everywhere with the help of a crusty
and unflappable street-wise gumshoe.
That’d make me the sidekick.
I’m good either way.
Okay, sidekick Avenger, without Superman’s
super finger, this is a whole different ball
game. This game’s all about the hustle.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 7.
CONTINUED:
I love the hustle!

scenes.heading: EXT. PAPEN COUNTY FOUNTAIN - DAY

lines.text: Emerson talks with a BEAT COP in the b.g., slips him some CASH,
then ducks under the CRIME SCENE TAPE and joins Chuck, who
stands not far from THE FOUNTAIN. A WOMAN’S BODY is half-in,
half-out. The CORONER, and a COUPLE HELPERS, stand with BLOW-
DRYERS, doing their best to melt the ice and extract the woman.
Body’s been identified off an employee ID card
for Dicker’s Department Store as Erin Embry.
EMERSON AND CHUCK’S POV - A HUGE, BRUISED BUMP is visible on
ERIN’S FOREHEAD.
(wrinkling her nose)
What’s that smell? It reminds me of Aunt Lily
on Sundays. I mean, my mother on Sundays.
Single-malt Scotch. Reminds me of something I
could use a snifter of right now. Cops are
saying this was an accident. Lady still in
the holiday spirit guzzles too many spirits,
pulls a Gene Kelly ‘round the rosy, slips,
bonks her noggin and falls into the fountain.
Which froze when the temperatures dipped
overnight. How awful.
What’s awful is this was a big, fat waste of
my time. There’s no case here.
Aw. But I’m not done doing the Hustle.
Then you gonna be dancing by yourself.
OMIT

scenes.heading: EXT. STREET - NIGHT

lines.text: Ned and Chuck hold hands (it’s winter, they wear gloves!) while
they walk PIGBY and DIGBY. Ned holds up Chuck’s hand in his as
she pulls him along, trailing close behind her.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 8.
CONTINUED:
But instead of dancing by herself, Chuck found
another partner for the Hustle.
(re: them holding hands)
Winter is my new best friend. We should move
to the South Pole. Although, I don’t know if
there’s much need for pie at the South Pole
and that would put a wrinkle in my newly-
starched life as a normal guy who makes pie.
I’d give it up, though, if it meant holding
your hand every day.
The pie or the normal?
Either, though I’d prefer to have my pie and
normal it, too. Where are we going?
Dicker’s Department Store. Erin Embry, that
poor woman who was murdered in the fountain,
she worked at Dicker’s.
“Murdered”? Thought her death was an accident.
It was dismissed as an accident. Murders are
dismissed as accidents everyday. My murder
coulda’ been dismissed as an accident. Coulda’
said I slipped and fell overboard when really I
was strangled and thrown overboard. I bet Erin
Embry was dead before she hit the water.
Just like you.
Just like me. I knew it!
What? What did you know?
Chuck indicates THE WINDOW DISPLAY: A replica of the Papen
County Fountain. A FEMALE MANNEQUIN holding A GLASS OF
CHAMPAGNE is tossing JEWELS into the fountain while making a
wish. Chuck studies it.
This looks like the fountain where Erin died.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 9.
CONTINUED: (2)
The Papen Fountain’s a pretty popular spot.
But does everyone who goes there to make a
wish wear the same exact outfit?
(re: the window)
This is the scene of the crime!
Yay for the Alive-Again Avenger!
NED / CHUCK
Yay!
Let’s go find Emerson and tell him that Erin
Embry’s murder is on display in a Dicker’s
Department Store window.
But I’m not an avenger. I’m a pie-maker. I
don’t wanna pretend to be something I’m not.
It’s stressful. So I’m gonna go back to the
Pie Hole and make my moniker proud.
Then I’m going to go avenge, and make my
moniker proud.
Who needs Superman? You’re my hero.
Chuck kisses her glove and holds Ned’s cheek a moment, leaving a
lipstick mark as if she kissed him herself.
While the Pie-Maker lingered on his Alive-
Again Avenger...

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - NIGHT

lines.text: TING-A-LING! RANDY MANN ENTERS carrying a TAXIDERMY SCULPTURE
of FRED & GINGER (the Great Herrmann’s doves from Episode 206)
FLYING OUT of a MAGICIAN’S TOP HAT. Randy sits at the counter.
...Randy Mann, a taxidermist who once paid for
friends until the Pie-Maker befriended him for
free, came to the Pie Hole bearing a gift, but
said gift wasn’t the first priority of his visit.
Hey, ho, pie-bro.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 10.
CONTINUED:
Olive stands behind the counter.
Who you calling “ho”? Oh. Randy Mann.
That priority was Olive Snook.
Miss Olive. Meant no offense by that “ho.”
Intent was to be jolly, not derogatory. Is
the Pie-Maker present? No? I’ll wait.
Can I get you a slice of pie?
As a supportive friend, I’d like to try them
all. One slice of everything, please.
Starting with your favorite of the day.
I’m not sure eating that much fruit is wise.
I’ll pace myself... and may be here awhile.
Dandy. Are those the birds Ned had you stuff?
Birthday gift for his magician brothers.
(stares at Olive, then)
What do you think? Magical enough?
Wow.
“Wow’s” good, right? “Wow” means you like it?
I’m gonna say yes. Declaratively. Boy, you
sure turned these birds around fast.
All in a few days’ sleepless work. When
you’re starting a new business venture, it’s
important not to keep the customer waiting.
More important to Randy Mann than keeping the
customer from waiting, was keeping himself
from waiting to see Olive Snook.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT ONE 11.
CONTINUED: (2)
TING-A-LING! In walk Jerry and Buster. They spot Olive.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
And he wasn’t the only person who couldn’t
wait to see Olive Snook...
Jiminy convicts!! Those are the guys who
kidnapped me when I was a little girl.
JERRY / BUSTER
SNOOK!
As Randy stands, ready to defend Olive at any cost...
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 12.
FADE IN:

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - NIGHT

lines.text: Ned ENTERS to see three men sitting at the counter, their backs
to him, Olive behind the counter.
Olive Snook had closed early, but not due to a
lackadaisical work ethic or lack of patrons.
As Jerry, Buster and Randy spin around, Ned notices the ICE PACK
to Randy’s face, which he drops, revealing a BLACK EYE.
Oh my God. Randy! Olive! Did you hit him?
Did she hit you?
(gestures to Jerry)
He did it. I have a low platelet count. And
zero percent body fat. That’s a one-two punch
for bruising. Ha -- that would be funny if I
hadn’t been the one who got punched.
I told you not to. I told him not to.
Sucker punch.
(in Jerry’s face)
Sucker punch!
Buster claps Randy on the back.
Take it easy, tough guy. Coulda’ been a whole
lot worse had we not seen you attempting to
shank us with chivalrous intention.
Olive, who are these guys?
Who are any of us, really?
They’re her childhood kidnappers.
They weren’t exactly “kidnappers.”
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 13.
CONTINUED:
What they were, exactly, was this:

scenes.heading: INT. CAR - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Young Jerry and Young Buster climb into the front seat of the
car. Jerry reaches under the dash and begins to hot-wire the
car. The ENGINE IGNITES and they throw the car into gear.
Jerry and Buster were petty thieves, but they
were not kidnappers. They were in the wrong
car at the wrong time and were not alone.
THE BACKSEAT:
Young Olive sits in the backseat next to a SUITCASE, unbeknownst
to either Jerry or Buster.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Young Olive Snook had stowed away in their
recently-stolen car. Hoping the old adage,
“Absence makes the heart grow fonder,” would
prove true, she wanted to teach her
neglectful parents a lesson.
Buster glances over his shoulder into the backseat and sees
Young Olive for the first time. He taps Jerry on the shoulder.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Jerry and Buster wanted to return the little
girl to her parents right away...
What’s your name, pickle?
...but, despite their attempts, she refused to
tell them her name.
Young Olive just stares with an excited smile.
OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. MOTEL ROOM - NIGHT - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Young Olive sits on a couch in the DARK ROOM. Jerry and Buster,
a PHONE RECEIVER held to their ears, are arguing in the b.g.
Their argument was hushed so Young Olive would
not hear that repeated calls to her parents
had gone unanswered...
ANGLE ON YOUNG OLIVE, who we REVEAL is WATCHING CARTOONS on TV.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 14.
CONTINUED:
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
...and so as not to disturb Olive’s love of
cartoons.
Jerry and Buster join Olive on the couch with a BIG BOWL OF
POPCORN. As the three watch and laugh, enjoying the show.

scenes.heading: EXT. YOUNG OLIVE’S HOUSE - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Young Olive walks slowly to the front door, glances back...
The 2 days, 12 hours and 19 minutes Young
Olive Snook spent with Jerry Holmes and Buster
Bustamante were the best 2 days, 12 hours and
19 minutes of her young life.
Jerry and Buster follow a few steps behind. They both smile.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
It was also the best of theirs.

scenes.heading: INT. YOUNG OLIVE’S HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: Jerry and Buster stand talking to Mom and Dad Snook.
After explaining the situation, the two men
realized Young Olive’s parents hadn’t even
known she was gone.
Jerry and Buster scold Mom and Dad Snook.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
They confronted the Snooks on their derelict
parenting skills. Mom and Dad Snook took
umbrage and called the authorities.

scenes.heading: EXT. YOUNG OLIVE’S HOUSE - DAY - FLASHBACK

lines.text: LOOKING UP. Young Olive stands in her bedroom window looking
down, Mom and Dad on either side.
As it was their word against the word of two
petty thieves, the now-accused kidnappers were
sent away for the maximum the law would allow.
YOUNG OLIVE’S POV - JERRY AND BUSTER ARE HANDCUFFED.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
Knowing what she’d lost the minute they were
gone, Young Olive vowed to keep in touch.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 15.
CONTINUED:
RESUME ON THE WINDOW. Mom and Dad lead Olive away. A beat,
then she reappears, smiles and waves to Jerry and Buster below.
NARRATOR (CONT’D)
She wrote them every week and never forgot.
And they, in turn, never forgot her.
Jerry and Buster wave back before being put into the COP CAR.

scenes.heading: INT. PIE HOLE - NIGHT

lines.text: Ned, Olive, Randy, Jerry and Buster, as before.
Did you just get out?
Just.
Escaped. The word following that “just”
should’ve been “escaped.”
He’s holding a grudge over the shiner.
(to Randy)
A grudge-holder, huh? I like you.
How wonderful that you came to see me.
(sotto, to Olive)
It won’t be wonderful when the police show
up looking for ex-cons and happen upon other
sorts of ex-people we’d rather they didn’t
happen upon.
Which is why we need our Snook, here, to help
get us across the border. If she’s amenable.
It’s the least I can do. You never should’ve
gone to jail, but no one would believe me that
I ran away.
Done and done, Snookerdoodle. What do we
always say about the past?
It makes an ass out of you and me.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 16.
CONTINUED:
That’s my girl.
Can we go back to “escaped from prison,” or am
I the only one that finds that troubling?
Who’s the worrywart?
That’s Ned. He owns the place.
The Pie-Maker? The Pie-Maker?
Um... Boys...
If this don’t make tunneling through three
miles of prison sewage worth every single gag.
(to Randy)
Nudge your grudge off-a’ that stool,
crankypants, so I can get a good look at the
baker man who’s gonna marry our little girl!
Randy reluctantly gets up as Jerry HUGS a bewildered Ned. Ned
tries to catch Olive’s eye, but she won’t look at him.
JERRY (CONT’D)
Her weekly letters were the one bright light
in our single-bulb cell, ain’t that the
almighty truth, Buster?
Sent like a message from the Big Man himself.
Randy’s confused, looks to Ned.
But I thought you were--
Um. Actually. Olive. And me. Me and Olive--
Olive looks at Ned, unable to say a word.
The Pie-Maker considered how the truth would
humiliate Olive and devastate the two sweet men
whose only happiness, after being wrongfully
imprisoned for a crime they didn’t commit, came
from knowing the little girl they loved most was
loved most by the Pie-Maker. So he said:
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 17.
CONTINUED: (2)
Me and Olive... love each other very much.
Ned takes her hand in his. Olive, confused, looks at Ned, then
clasps her fingers around his and returns the smile.
And once again, Olive’s dream came true...
just not quite how she intended.
OMIT

scenes.heading: EXT. DICKER’S DEPARTMENT STORE - THE NEXT MORNING

lines.text: A GROUP set up a VIGIL honoring Erin Embry: FLOWERS, CANDLES,
PICTURES, etc. Emerson and Chuck study the vigil-holders.
Olive told me all about Jerry and Buster.
During our late-night girl-talks, we mostly
talk about Olive ‘cause, well, I’m an all-or-
nothing girl and I really can’t tell her the--
Emerson closes his eyes and begins to SNORE, then:
Pee-Wee mention she was tellin’ Papa 1 and Papa
2 that your man isn’t your man, he’s hers?
No, she didn’t. And now that she’s borrowed
him from my lending library of significant
others, I’m a little peeved.
Lending pie-boyfriend to your bestie who’s in
love with him so she can pull the wool over
her fake pops’ peepers is the sort of idea
that gives a bad idea the will to live.
That’s why I’m peeved! I can’t avenge when
I’m peeved. It splits my focus.
You’re no good to me focusing on lady peeves.
Focus on--
Now Ned and Olive are on a romantic run for
the border to champion the wrongfully accused
and... oh, I don’t know what I’m upset about.
It’s just for one day. I’m being ridiculous.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 18.
CONTINUED:
Mmm-hmm. A lot can happen in one day.
(re: the window)
This the last repose of Erin Embry?
Chuck’s still thinking about that “a lot can happen” comment.
That’s my theory.
Nice hustle, sidekick Avenger. Tummy’s
telling me Erin Embry wasn’t just some
spritzer girl annoying people with perfume.
A MAN, WENDELL FEATHERSTONE, overhears them and responds:
Erin wasn’t annoying people, she was dazzling
them with fantastic worlds created within the
proscenium arch of the Dicker’s window frame.
Erin Embry dressed this window?
With her partner, Coco Juniper. Although it
was common knowledge that Erin was the one
with the true talent. Erin could do things
with her mannequin Coco could never do.
What sort of things could Olive do that--?
Chuck gasps as she realizes what just came out of her mouth.
You saw their holiday window? “Christmas in
Bangkok.” The detail. Erin dressed tuk-tuk
drivers in platinum Santa hats. And do you
have any idea how long it takes to cut a
string of dolls representing the population of
Bangkok? Out of fur? Coarse fur? Erin did.
Who are you people?
We’re devotees. Fans of Erin’s and, to a
lesser extent, Coco’s, but we prefer the
term “devotee.”
Emerson pulls Chuck aside.
PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT TWO 19.
CONTINUED: (2)
Any of these devotees seem overly devoted?
Appropriately devoted. And overly devastated
by Erin’s death, which is about to be avenged.

OFF that...

lines.text: Chuck and Emerson (who is counting his cash) approach storeowner

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Olive and Ned turn to each other and, hesitantly, but doing

OLIVE’S VOICE

(singing)

PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT THREE 30.
CONTINUED:
The craft and beauty of Dicker’s signature

(no response)
Coco?

Dick takes out a REMOTE CONTROL, LIFTS IT IN TRIBUTE.
DICK DICKER (CONT’D)
This is truly an honor.

Please join Coco and myself inside for a

Ohmygod!

PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 32.

OMIT

scenes.heading: INT. CHUCK’S AUNTS’ HOUSE - CHEESE ROOM - NIGHT

scenes.heading: INT. DICKER’S DEPARTMENT STORE - MANNEQUIN ROOM - NIGHT

PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 35.

PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 37.

PUSHING DAISIES #211 "Window Dressed To Kill" 10/26/08 FINAL DRAFT ACT FOUR 38.
